system: common law system, based on English model, with special legislation and land courts for the Maori

constitution.history: New Zealand has no single constitution document; the Constitution Act 1986, effective 1 January 1987, includes only part of the uncodified constitution; others include a collection of statutes or "acts of Parliament," the Treaty of Waitangi, Orders in Council, letters patent, court decisions, and unwritten conventions
constitution.amend: proposed as bill by Parliament or by referendum called either by the government or by citizens; passage of a bill as an act normally requires two separate readings with committee reviews in between to make changes and corrections, a third reading approved by the House of Representatives membership or by the majority of votes in a referendum, and assent of the governor-general; passage of amendments to reserved constitutional provisions affecting the term of Parliament, electoral districts, and voting restrictions requires approval by 75% of the House membership or the majority of votes in a referendum

courts.highest: Supreme Court (consists of 5 justices, including the chief justice)
courts.judges: justices appointed by the governor-general upon the recommendation of the attorney- general; justices appointed until compulsory retirement at age 70
courts.lower: Court of Appeal; High Court; tribunals and authorities; district courts; specialized courts for issues related to employment, environment, family, Maori lands, youth, military; tribunals

citizenship.descent: at least one parent must be a citizen of New Zealand

world: accepts compulsory ICJ jurisdiction with reservations; accepts ICCt jurisdiction

gov.type: parliamentary democracy under a constitutional monarchy; a Commonwealth realm

executive.chosen: the monarchy is hereditary; governor-general appointed by the monarch on the advice of the prime minister; following legislative elections, the governor-general appoints the leader of the majority party or majority coalition as prime minister; deputy prime minister also appointed by the governor-general
executive.cabinet: Executive Council appointed by the governor-general on the recommendation of the prime minister

b: Importing illegal drugs could result in a prison sentence of up to 12 years.
